newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: AUA sees cap increase without state-report.
newsitem.headline: AUA sees cap increase without state-report.

text.p: Austrian Airlines expects to carry out a planned 400 million schillings capital increase next year, without the participation of majority shareholder the Austrian state, AUA director Herbert Bammer said.
"Given the current budget situation, it is more likely that the state will not take part," Bammer was quoted as saying in an interview with Der Standard newspaper.

Austria's flag carrier has authorisation to raise its capital to three billion schillings from 2.6 billion by the end of 1998. If the state does not participate, its AUA stake will fall to 45 percent from 51.9 percent.
The finance ministry has so far declined comment on its plans.
Bammer ruled out issuing the new share capital this year because of low interest rates.
Under AUA's existing shareholder structure, Swissair has a stake of around 10 percent and All Nippon Airways nine percent. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
